pilot: PILOT -- open-ended instrument validation on dev subjects; no research conclusions.
purpose: Owner >=50-label judge spot-check (PILOT_SPEC section 7, precondition 6). Do not open until the labels are written.
shortfall_note: PILOT_SPEC section 7 asks for 50 calls balanced 25 SAME / 25 DIFFERENT 'where supply allows (shortfall filled with UNCLEAR and said so)'. Supply does not allow 25 DIFFERENT here. Across both scored models and all five arms the item set yields 37 DIFFERENT labels in total, and 9 of the 17 items have ZERO DIFFERENT labels anywhere. The standing twin rule caps the sample at one row per item per sheet, so the ceiling on DIFFERENT rows is 23. The remainder is filled with UNCLEAR and is named here rather than quietly rebalanced.
blinding: Sheets carry no arm, no model and no judge label. The mapping lives only in this file.
twin_rule: STANDING EVAL RULE (D6-v4.9), added 2026-07-27 after the frontier rater named TWIN-PAIR STANCE INFERENCE as one of six tells on round 3's detectability sheet: no rater and no scorer may ever see both twins of a duplicated question. Round 3's sheet showed five questions twice, once as a real entry and once as a control; the option sets shared nothing, so elimination was impossible, but a reader could still reason across the two stance sets. The rule generalises that: within any single prompt file or rating sheet a question appears AT MOST ONCE. Asserted at export, not assumed.

entries.judge_why: The REAL answer commits to supporting a nationalist movement in the context of the Syrian civil war ("Yes, I believe there is... the focal point of our support should be in the area of civilian protection"), whereas the CANDIDATE answer redefines the question to address Western populist nationalism ("Whether it is here in the States or across Europe, we are seeing a massive awakening").

The REAL answer states that exposure to violence "is related to a number of later outcomes, including increased involvement in violence itself" and "lower abilities... in terms of schooling," while the CANDIDATE answer similarly claims it "affects their ability to concentrate in school" and "creates a cycle of instability that makes them more vulnerable to the very violence they witnessed."

The REAL answer notes that "the military as an institution receives a great deal of aid from the United States" but must balance this with the fact that "the United States needs Egypt more," while the CANDIDATE similarly claims that an Egyptian government "has to take the American reaction into account" but must perform "a delicate balancing act between maintaining strategic foreign alliances and satisfying domestic political expectations."

The REAL answer states "it's really hard to disentangle... it's kind of a vicious cycle" and the CANDIDATE similarly rejects the "linear, 'chicken and egg' thinking and instead look[s] at it as a set of reinforcing dynamics."

The REAL answer claims there is a majority "not to stop Brexit, but to go for a different form of Brexit," whereas the CANDIDATE answer claims politicians are "sleepwalking toward a cliff" because no one has the courage to say "we made a terrible mistake" and back away.

The REAL answer discusses Iran's nuclear enrichment timeline ("it all depends on Iranian behavior and how fast they push the nuclear program"), whereas the CANDIDATE answer addresses a completely different topic regarding Israeli-Palestinian peace negotiations ("leaders like Netanyahu or Abbas").

The REAL answer states "this has certainly aggravated the problem" by giving adversaries "a free ride," whereas the CANDIDATE answer argues that "To suggest that a different set of American policies would have cleanly resolved a civil war of this magnitude oversimplifies a profoundly difficult reality."
The REAL answer states there is "No doubt whatsoever" that Sisi could win, while the CANDIDATE answer similarly concludes "it is very difficult to see a credible path for any other outcome."

The REAL answer suggests the election result could "turn out to be good, better, less bad" because "this election result would legitimize a different approach," whereas the CANDIDATE answer states "it is very difficult to see how this could be viewed as a positive" and warns "we shall pay a heavy price for this."
